sections.title: Advanced Concept
sections.content: Level 2 focuses on multi-group and weighted averages, missing values, combined averages, and consecutive numbers with gaps. The basic formula remains the same: Average = Sum / Count, but applied in multi-step problems.

sections.title: Weighted Averages
sections.content: When different groups have different sizes, the combined average depends on group sizes. Formula: Combined Average = (n1×A1 + n2×A2 + ... + nk×Ak) / (n1+n2+...+nk). Example: Class A (10 students, avg 50), Class B (15 students, avg 60) → Combined avg = (10×50 + 15×60)/25 = 56.

sections.title: Missing Observations in Groups
sections.content: When multiple numbers are missing, first calculate total sum using average × total count, then subtract known numbers. Example: Avg of 6 numbers = 40, known numbers = 35, 45, 50 → Sum of known = 130 → Sum of missing = 6×40 - 130 = 110 → Missing numbers sum = 110.

sections.title: Change in Average After Adding/Removing Numbers
sections.content: When numbers are added or removed, new average = (Old Sum ± Sum of Added/Removed) / New Count. Example: Avg of 5 numbers = 20 → Add 30 → New avg = (20×5 + 30)/6 = 22.5.

sections.title: Relation with Total Sum
sections.content: Sum = Average × Count. This helps in solving group comparisons, replacements, or successive changes problems quickly.

sections.title: Average of Consecutive Numbers
sections.content: For consecutive numbers, average = (First + Last) / 2. For n numbers, average = middle value (odd n) or mean of two middle numbers (even n).

sections.title: Average after Replacing Numbers
sections.content: When a number is replaced, new average = Old average + (New number - Replaced number)/Total count. Example: Avg of 4 numbers = 25 → Replace 30 with 40 → New avg = 25 + (40-30)/4 = 27.5.

sections.title: Handling Different Units or Values
sections.content: For averages involving different weights or units (e.g., kg, ₹), always convert to common unit first and then apply sum/count.

tricks.title: Weighted Average Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Multiply each group average by group size, sum, divide by total size.
tricks.example: 5 students avg 40, 10 students avg 60 → Combined avg = (5×40 + 10×60)/15 = 53.33.

tricks.title: Missing Number Quick Formula
tricks.explanation: Missing = (Total Avg × Total count) - Sum of known numbers.

tricks.title: Replacement Trick
tricks.explanation: New avg = Old avg + (New value - Replaced value)/Total count.

tricks.title: Adding/Removing Numbers Shortcut
tricks.explanation: New avg = (Old sum ± Sum of new/removed numbers)/New count.

tricks.title: Average of Consecutive Numbers
tricks.explanation: Average = (First + Last)/2 or middle number for odd series.

tricks.title: Combining Multiple Groups
tricks.explanation: Consider each group separately with its size × average, sum and divide by total.

tricks.title: Quick Check Using Deviations
tricks.explanation: Sum of deviations from average = 0, helps verify calculations quickly.

tricks.title: Estimating Average
tricks.explanation: Round numbers for quick approximation before detailed calculation.

tricks.title: Adjusting Average After Scaling
tricks.explanation: If all numbers are multiplied by k, new avg = old avg × k.

tricks.title: Adjusting Average After Adding Constant
tricks.explanation: Add constant c to all numbers → New avg = old avg + c.
tricks.example: Avg 20 → Add 5 to each → New avg = 25.
